T: Fate has a plan. So does dessert.
D: A politician falls for a dancer while mysterious men try to keep them apart.
P: Serve the snacks when David meets Elise on the bus.
S: from the cart beside the bus stop
Mixed nuts tossed with honey, butter, sugar and a pinch of cinnamon, roasted at 170C until glossy, poured into paper cones.
keep your hat on, it opens the doors

Toasted baguette slices with whipped goat's cheese (beaten with a little cream), warm honey, thyme and cracked pepper. Cut half a baguette, about 150g, into 8 slices. Toast at 200°C conventional for 5 to 7 minutes until golden. Beat 120g soft goat's cheese with 30ml thickened cream until light. Warm 30g honey gently for 30 seconds. Spread the cheese on the toast, drizzle with warm honey and finish with 1 tsp thyme leaves and 1/4 tsp cracked black pepper.
the hotel bathroom where they first meet
Thick cucumber rounds with smoked salmon, a dot of crème fraîche whipped with lemon, dill and black pepper.
M: the date they're not supposed to have
Sirloin seared hard and rested, sliced, with shallot and red wine butter melting over the top and double-fried frites.
Lobster tails cut through the shell, sautéed with garlic, chilli and cherry tomatoes, white wine, linguine finished in the sauce.
W: the plan says it melts in the middle

Melt 125g dark chocolate with 125g butter, whisk in 2 eggs, 2 yolks and 60g sugar, fold in 30g flour, bake buttered moulds at 200C for 10 minutes. Butter four 150ml moulds using 10g extra butter. Heat the oven to 200°C conventional. Melt 125g dark chocolate with 125g butter gently and cool slightly. Whisk 2 whole eggs and 2 yolks with 60g caster sugar until pale. Stir in the chocolate mixture, then fold in 30g plain flour. Divide among the moulds and bake for 10 minutes until the edges are set and centres remain soft. Rest 1 minute, loosen the edges and carefully turn onto plates. Serve immediately.
K: election night, win or lose, the night David meets Elise

Gin shaken with lemon and sugar syrup, poured into flutes and topped with brut champagne and a long lemon twist. Dissolve 40g caster sugar in 40ml hot water and cool. Shake 120ml gin, 60ml lemon juice and 40ml syrup with ice for 10 seconds. Strain evenly into 4 chilled flutes. Top each with 90ml cold brut champagne, pouring slowly. Finish with a long strip of lemon peel.

s.note: Mixed nuts roasted glossy with honey, butter and cinnamon.
s.how: Melt 30g butter with 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp brown sugar, a pinch of cinnamon and 1/2 tsp salt. Toss through 300g mixed nuts, spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes, stirring halfway. Cool for 5 minutes so they crisp, then pour into paper cones.

s.note: Toasted baguette slices with whipped goat's cheese (beaten with a little cream), warm honey, thyme and cracked pepper.
s.how: Cut half a baguette, about 150g, into 8 slices. Toast at 200°C conventional for 5 to 7 minutes until golden. Beat 120g soft goat's cheese with 30ml thickened cream until light. Warm 30g honey gently for 30 seconds. Spread the cheese on the toast, drizzle with warm honey and finish with 1 tsp thyme leaves and 1/4 tsp cracked black pepper.

m.note: Seared sirloin, shallot red wine butter and double fried frites.
m.how: Finely dice 2 shallots and simmer with 80ml red wine in a small pan for 8 minutes until almost dry. Cool, then mix into 60g softened butter with a pinch of salt. Chill. Cut 800g potatoes into frites, rinse and dry thoroughly. Fry in neutral oil at 140°C for 5 minutes, drain and cool 15 minutes; fry again at 185°C for 3 minutes until crisp. Salt lightly. Season four 200g sirloin steaks, sear hard in a hot pan with 1 tbsp oil for about 3 minutes each side to your preferred doneness, then rest 8 minutes. Slice and top with the shallot red wine butter; serve with frites.
